slides.title: Memory Management Best Practices
slides.prompt: Modern C++ memory management principles mandate avoiding raw new/delete in application code. Leverage smart pointers, RAII containers, sanitizers (ASan), and Valgrind to ensure zero memory leaks.
slides.codeSnippet:
// Modern C++ Rule: Avoid raw 'new' and 'delete'!
auto data = std::make_unique<std::vector<int>>(1000);

slides.title: AddressSanitizer Compiler Flag
slides.prompt: Fill in the GCC/Clang compiler flag used to enable runtime AddressSanitizer memory leak detection.

slides.title: Rule of Zero
slides.prompt: What does the 'Rule of Zero' state in modern C++ guidelines?
options: Classes relying on RAII smart pointers and containers should define ZERO custom destructors or copy/move operations
Classes must contain zero pointer variables
All functions should return zero on success
slides.correctAnswer: Classes relying on RAII smart pointers and containers should define ZERO custom destructors or copy/move operations

slides.title: Leak Detection Tool
slides.prompt: Fill in the popular Linux profiling framework tool used with Memcheck to detect C++ memory leaks.

slides.title: Double Free Fault Definition
slides.prompt: What error causes a 'double free' runtime fault?
options: Attempting to call delete/free twice on the same heap memory address
Allocating memory inside a loop 2 times
Failing to close a smart pointer
slides.correctAnswer: Attempting to call delete/free twice on the same heap memory address

slides.title: Undefined Behavior Prevention
slides.prompt: Fill in the smart pointer to select by default when exclusive single ownership is required.

slides.title: Deprecated auto_ptr
slides.prompt: Why was std::auto_ptr removed in C++17?
options: Its broken copy-semantics silently transferred ownership, causing subtle bugs and unsafe container usage
It ran too slowly on multi-core processors
It did not support template parameters
slides.correctAnswer: Its broken copy-semantics silently transferred ownership, causing subtle bugs and unsafe container usage

slides.title: LeakSanitizer Flag
slides.prompt: Fill in the standalone sanitizer flag targeted specifically at detecting memory leaks.

slides.title: Passing Smart Pointers to Functions
slides.prompt: What is the recommended best practice for passing an object to a function that only needs to read it without sharing ownership?
options: Pass by const reference (const T&) or raw pointer/reference derived via .get()
Convert to std::weak_ptr and pass by value
slides.correctAnswer: Pass by const reference (const T&) or raw pointer/reference derived via .get()
